description: This majestic Middle Eastern Lamb Ouzi features a whole lamb, slow roasted to succulent perfection, served atop a fragrant bed of spiced rice. A truly impressive dish, it promises a feast of tender meat and aromatic flavors, ideal for grand celebrations. Prepare to delight your guests with this unforgettable culinary masterpiece.

instructions.title: Prepare the Lamb
instructions.text: Pat the lamb dry. In a small bowl, combine 2 tablespoons olive oil, 1 teaspoon salt, 1 teaspoon black pepper, 1 teaspoon allspice, 1/2 teaspoon cinnamon, 1/4 teaspoon cardamom, and 1/8 teaspoon nutmeg. Rub this spice mixture generously all over the lamb shoulder or leg. Cover and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes, or preferably overnight.

instructions.title: Slow Roast the Lamb
instructions.text: Preheat your oven to 325F (160C). Place the marinated lamb in a large roasting pan. Add 2 cups of lamb broth or water to the bottom of the pan. Cover the pan tightly with foil or a lid. Roast for 3 to 4 hours, or until the lamb is fall-off-the-bone tender. Baste occasionally with the pan juices. For the last 30 minutes, remove the foil to allow the lamb to brown slightly.

instructions.title: Prepare the Rice Base
instructions.text: While the lamb is roasting, melt 1 tablespoon butter and 1 tablespoon olive oil in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium heat. Add the chopped onion and cook until softened, about 5-7 minutes. Add the minced garlic and cook for another minute until fragrant. Stir in the remaining allspice, cinnamon, cardamom, nutmeg, salt, and pepper.

instructions.title: Cook the Ouzi Rice
instructions.text: Add the rinsed basmati rice to the pot with the onions and spices, stirring to coat the grains. Pour in the remaining 4 cups of lamb broth or water. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 15 minutes, or until the liquid is absorbed and the rice is tender. Stir in the green peas and diced carrots, then cover and let it steam for another 5 minutes.

instructions.title: Toast Nuts and Assemble
instructions.text: In a small pan, toast the pine nuts and slivered almonds over medium heat until golden brown and fragrant, being careful not to burn them. Once the lamb is done, carefully remove it from the roasting pan and let it rest on a cutting board, covered loosely with foil. Fluff the rice gently with a fork.

instructions.title: Serve Your Lamb Ouzi
instructions.text: To serve, spread the fragrant Ouzi rice onto a large serving platter. Carefully place the whole slow-roasted lamb on top of the rice. Garnish generously with the toasted pine nuts, slivered almonds, and fresh chopped parsley. Serve immediately with a side of yogurt or tzatziki, if desired. Enjoy the tender, flavorful meat and aromatic rice.

tips: For even more flavor, marinate the lamb overnight. This allows the spices to deeply penetrate the meat, resulting in a more aromatic and tender roast.
Do not overcrowd the roasting pan. Ensure there is enough space around the lamb for even cooking and browning. If your lamb is very large, consider a larger pan or cutting it into a couple of pieces.

To achieve perfectly fluffy rice, resist the urge to lift the lid while it simmers. Let it rest for a few minutes after cooking before fluffing, which allows the steam to redistribute and grains to separate.
article:
Embark on a culinary journey to the heart of the Middle East, where food is not just sustenance but a celebration of family, tradition, and exquisite flavors. Among the most revered dishes gracing grand tables is Lamb Ouzi, a spectacular whole slow roasted lamb dish that promises an unforgettable dining experience. This isn't just a meal; it's an event, a centerpiece that embodies generosity and the rich tapestry of Middle Eastern hospitality. Prepare to impress your guests and delight your palate with this comprehensive guide to creating a truly authentic and succulent Lamb Ouzi feast.

## What is Lamb Ouzi?

Lamb Ouzi, sometimes spelled "Ozzy" or "Ozi," is a majestic Middle Eastern dish, typically served at weddings, Eid celebrations, and other significant gatherings. At its core, it features a whole, or a large cut, of lamb that has been slow-roasted to absolute perfection, resulting in incredibly tender, fall-off-the-bone meat. This succulent lamb is then often served atop a bed of fragrant, spiced basmati rice, studded with toasted nuts like almonds and pine nuts, and sometimes garnished with raisins or fresh herbs. The beauty of Lamb Ouzi lies in its simplicity of ingredients combined with the mastery of slow cooking, allowing the lamb's natural flavors to deepen and meld with aromatic spices. It's a dish that demands patience but rewards with unparalleled taste and a truly spectacular presentation.

## Ingredients for Whole Slow Roasted Lamb Ouzi

Crafting the perfect Lamb Ouzi requires quality ingredients and a thoughtful approach to seasoning. Here’s what you’ll need to create this Middle Eastern masterpiece:

For the Whole Lamb (or large cut like a leg or shoulder, 8-10 lbs):
*   1 whole lamb (or large cut), bone-in (approx. 8-10 lbs)
*   1/2 cup olive oil
*   1/4 cup lemon juice
*   1/4 cup white vinegar
*   1/4 cup plain yogurt (optional, for tenderizing)
*   8-10 cloves garlic, minced
*   2 tbsp ground cumin
*   2 tbsp ground coriander
*   1 tbsp sweet paprika
*   1 tbsp ground allspice
*   1 tsp ground black pepper
*   1 tsp ground cinnamon
*   1/2 tsp ground cardamom
*   Salt to taste (approximately 2-3 tbsp)
*   Fresh rosemary and thyme sprigs (optional, for cavity)

For the Spiced Rice:
*   4 cups basmati rice, rinsed until water runs clear
*   8 cups lamb or chicken broth
*   1/4 cup olive oil or ghee
*   2 large onions, finely chopped
*   4-5 cloves garlic, minced
*   1 tbsp ground allspice
*   1 tsp ground cinnamon
*   1/2 tsp ground cardamom
*   1/2 tsp ground black pepper
*   Salt to taste

For the Garnish:
*   1/2 cup slivered almonds, toasted
*   1/2 cup pine nuts, toasted
*   1/2 cup chopped fresh parsley or mint
*   Optional: 1/2 cup golden raisins, soaked in warm water

## Step-by-Step Instructions for Lamb Ouzi

Preparing a whole slow roasted Lamb Ouzi is a labor of love, but each step contributes to its magnificent outcome.

1.  **Prepare the Lamb:** Pat the lamb dry thoroughly with paper towels. Using a sharp knife, score the fatty parts of the lamb in a crosshatch pattern, being careful not to cut too deep into the meat. In a large bowl, whisk together the olive oil, lemon juice, vinegar, yogurt (if using), minced garlic, cumin, coriander, paprika, allspice, black pepper, cinnamon, cardamom, and salt to create a rich marinade.
2.  **Marinate the Lamb:** Rub the marinade generously all over the lamb, ensuring it gets into the scored cuts. If using, place rosemary and thyme sprigs inside the cavity. Place the lamb in a large roasting pan, cover it tightly with plastic wrap, and refrigerate for at least 12 hours, preferably 24 hours, to allow the flavors to penetrate deeply.
3.  **Preheat and Roast:** Preheat your oven to a low temperature, around 300°F (150°C). Remove the lamb from the refrigerator and let it come to room temperature for about an hour. Cover the roasting pan tightly with aluminum foil, ensuring no steam escapes.
4.  **Slow Roast:** Place the covered lamb in the preheated oven. Roast for 4-6 hours, or until the lamb is incredibly tender and easily pulls away from the bone. The exact time will depend on the size of your lamb and your oven. For the last 30-45 minutes, remove the foil to allow the skin to crisp up and brown.
5.  **Rest the Lamb:** Once cooked, remove the lamb from the oven, transfer it to a large cutting board, and tent it loosely with foil. Let it rest for at least 30 minutes before carving. This allows the juices to redistribute, ensuring a more succulent meat.
6.  **Prepare the Spiced Rice:** While the lamb is resting, prepare the rice. In a large pot or Dutch oven, heat the olive oil or ghee over medium heat. Add the chopped onions and sauté until softened and translucent, about 5-7 minutes. Add the minced garlic and cook for another minute until fragrant.
7.  **Cook the Rice:** Stir in the allspice, cinnamon, cardamom, black pepper, and salt. Add the rinsed basmati rice and stir to coat evenly with the spices. Pour in the lamb or chicken broth. Bring to a boil, then reduce the heat to low, cover tightly, and simmer for 15-20 minutes, or until all the liquid has been absorbed and the rice is tender. Turn off the heat and let the rice steam, covered, for another 10 minutes. Fluff with a fork.
8.  **Assemble and Garnish:** To serve your Lamb Ouzi, create a grand presentation. Spread the spiced rice onto a large serving platter. Carefully transfer the whole roasted lamb onto the center of the rice. Garnish generously with toasted slivered almonds, pine nuts, fresh parsley or mint, and optional golden raisins.

## Pro Tips for the Best Lamb Ouzi

*   **Quality Lamb:** Start with a good quality, fresh lamb. A young lamb will be more tender. If using a whole lamb, ensure it fits your oven and roasting pan.
*   **Marination is Key:** Don't skimp on marination time. The longer the lamb marinates, the more flavorful and tender it will become. 24 hours is ideal.
*   **Low and Slow:** The secret to truly tender lamb is a low oven temperature and a long cooking time. This breaks down the connective tissues slowly, resulting in fall-off-the-bone meat.
*   **Tight Seal:** When roasting, ensure your roasting pan is tightly sealed with foil. This traps moisture and steam, essentially braising the lamb in its own juices and marinade.
*   **Resting Period:** Do not skip the resting period. It’s crucial for the juices to redistribute throughout the meat, making it incredibly moist and flavorful.
*   **Toasting Nuts:** Toasting the almonds and pine nuts brings out their nutty flavor and adds a delightful crunch to the dish. Do this gently in a dry pan until lightly golden.

## Serving Suggestions for Your Ouzi Feast

Lamb Ouzi is a complete meal in itself, but it truly shines when accompanied by a few complementary side dishes that balance its richness.

*   **Yogurt Sauce:** A simple cucumber and mint yogurt (tzatziki or labneh) provides a refreshing counterpoint to the rich lamb.
*   **Fresh Salad:** A crisp Arabic salad (salata baladi) with tomatoes, cucumbers, onions, and a lemon-tahini dressing offers freshness and tang.
*   **Hummus and Pita:** Classic hummus with warm pita bread is always a welcome addition, perfect for scooping up any extra rice or lamb drippings.
*   **Pickles:** Assorted Middle Eastern pickles (torshi) add a delightful sour crunch that cuts through the richness.

## Variations and Substitutions for Lamb Ouzi

While the traditional Lamb Ouzi uses a whole lamb, there are practical variations for home cooks:

*   **Lamb Cut:** Instead of a whole lamb, a bone-in lamb leg or shoulder (around 5-7 lbs) works beautifully and is more manageable for most home ovens. Adjust roasting time accordingly.
*   **Spice Blend:** While the listed spices are traditional, feel free to adjust to your preference. A touch of dried lime (loomi) or bay leaves can be added to the roasting pan for extra depth.
*   **Rice Variations:** For a different texture, you can use a mix of basmati rice and small pasta like orzo or vermicelli (toasted before adding to the rice). Some versions also include ground lamb or beef cooked into the rice for an even heartier dish.
*   **Vegetarian Ouzi:** While not traditional Ouzi, a vegetarian version can be made by using a large roasted cauliflower or eggplant as a centerpiece, served over the same spiced rice and garnished with nuts.
*   **Stuffing:** Some elaborate Ouzi recipes involve stuffing the lamb cavity with a mixture of spiced rice, ground meat, and nuts before roasting, creating an even more impressive dish.

## Frequently Asked Questions About Lamb Ouzi

**Q: Can I prepare Lamb Ouzi ahead of time?**
A: Yes, you can marinate the lamb up to 2 days in advance. The spiced rice can also be cooked a few hours ahead and gently reheated. The nuts can be toasted ahead of time as well. For best results, roast the lamb on the day of serving.

**Q: What if I don't have a roasting pan large enough for a whole lamb?**
A: If you're using a whole lamb, you might need to find a heavy-duty disposable aluminum roasting pan, often available at catering supply stores or large supermarkets. Alternatively, opt for a large cut like a lamb leg or shoulder, which fits most standard roasting pans.

**Q: How do I know when the lamb is done?**
A: The lamb should be incredibly tender, easily pulling away from the bone with a fork. An internal temperature probe inserted into the thickest part of the meat (avoiding the bone) should read around 190-205°F (88-96°C) for fall-off-the-bone tenderness.

**Q: Can I use a pressure cooker for the lamb?**
A: While a pressure cooker can tenderize lamb quickly, it won't replicate the deep, complex flavors and the beautiful crispy exterior achieved through slow roasting. For true Lamb Ouzi, slow roasting is highly recommended.

**Q: What kind of rice is best for Ouzi?**
A: Long-grain basmati rice is ideal for Ouzi due to its fragrant aroma and fluffy texture when cooked. Rinse it thoroughly before cooking to remove excess starch, which prevents stickiness.

Bringing a whole slow roasted Lamb Ouzi to your table is more than just cooking; it's an act of culinary artistry and a tribute to rich Middle Eastern traditions. With patience, quality ingredients, and these detailed instructions, you can recreate this magnificent feast in your own home, creating memories around a truly spectacular meal. Enjoy the journey and the incredible flavors!
